description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/kvhslice.t's
inline `ok(1,"SKIP")` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p30-kvslice-scalar.pl) -- NO string eval anywhere:

    no warnings;
    my %h = map { $_ => uc $_ } 'a'..'z';
    print scalar(%h{'c','d','e'}), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  E     (a slice in scalar context yields its LAST element,
                       and a kv-slice's last element is the VALUE)
  PCL:          6     (the length of the flattened k,v,k,v,k,v list)

6 is a plausible number, which is why it reads as working.

THE ATTRIBUTION IN THE DOCS IS WRONG.  docs/not-supported.md 'Context
propagation into string eval' ends "**Affected tests:** perl-tests/kvhslice.t
tests 9-12 and 25-28 (scalar-context warning via `scalar eval '...'`)", and
the inline skip in the file said the same ("requires context propagation
through string eval, which PCL cannot do").  The probe above uses no eval at
all and still gives 6, so the eval gap is not the cause and cannot be what
closes these rows.  Correct the Affected-tests line when this is fixed.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/kvhslice.t 9 'last element in scalar context'
(got '6', want 'E'), 11 (got '0', want '2'), 28 (got undef, want 'a'), 29 (got
undef, want 'A').  Its neighbours 10, 12, 26, 27 are the WARNING half
("%h{...} in scalar context better written as $h{...}") and belong to #221,
not here.  Restored s464ay; these four are in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv with
this task as their cause, the four warning rows are skip-registered.

RELATED: rows 28/29 also need #1024 (a BAREWORD key inside `%h{...}` is not
autoquoted and is called as a sub), so they will not go green on this alone.

FIX SHAPE (untried): perl's rule is uniform -- a LIST in scalar context is its
last element, and PCL already gets that right for a value slice (`@h{...}`)
and for a list literal.  The kv-slice lowering appears to reach a
count-in-scalar-context path instead (the hash-in-boolean-context rule), so
the fix is to give `p-kv-hslice` the same scalar-context reduction its
sibling slices use.  Check the sibling `%a[...]` key/value ARRAY slice at the
same time -- kvaslice.t is a DIFF file in the companion suite (23/15).

=== CLOSED (s473t6c, 2026-09-19) ===

The task's own reproducer now agrees with perl in every spelling probed:

    my %h = (a=>'A',b=>'B',c=>'C',d=>'D',e=>'E');
    scalar(%h{'c','d','e'})              perl E        PCL E
    my $x = %h{'c','d','e'}              perl E        PCL E
    (%h{'c','d','e'}) in list context    perl cCdDeE   PCL cCdDeE
    sub f { scalar(%h{'c','d','e'}) }    perl E        PCL E

FIXED BY #1923: a kv-slice is a LIST like every other slice, so in scalar
context it is its LAST element, and `_slice_in_context_form` -- which
`@h{...}` and `@a[...]` already went through -- now wraps the two kv emitters
too.  The task's suspicion was right, and so was its "NOT the eval-context gap
docs/not-supported.md blames for it" note.

WHAT IS LEFT IS SOMEONE ELSE'S: perl-tests/kvhslice.t rows 9 and 11 still
fail, and they are `scalar eval"%h{'c','d','e'}"` -- the LAST EXPRESSION of a
string eval is emitted in LIST context whatever the call site is.  The PLAIN
slice `@h{...}` inside an eval is wrong the same way (3 vs E), and both are
right with no eval, so it is not a kv-slice fact.  Filed as #1943; both rows
now carry it.
subject: SILENT WRONG: a key/value hash slice `%h{...}` in SCALAR context yields the element COUNT, not the last VALUE -- `scalar(%h{'c','d','e'})` is 6 in PCL and 'E' in perl; NOT the eval-context gap docs/not-supported.md blames for it
